items.title: PCRS and NHS Wales primary care respiratory update, Cardiff, 20 October 2026
items.summary: PCRS is running a one-day essential primary care respiratory update in Cardiff on Tuesday 20 October 2026, with NHS Wales Performance and Improvement and members of the National Respiratory Audit Programme. A concentrated Welsh primary care respiratory audience.

items.title: Overall global sum down by £139m as over one million GP patients removed from lists
items.summary: New NHS England figures showed more than a million patients have now been removed from GP practice lists in England since a nationwide list-cleansing exercise began last October.

items.title: A clear message on vaping: holding two truths at once
items.summary: While new evidence strengthens the case for nicotine vapes as an effective smoking cessation aid, a major review highlights the risks for children and young people. In this clinical feature, Darush Attar-Zadeh and Nazir Hussain stress that for nurses the task is to communicate both messages clearly at the same time.

items.title: GPs keen to add data to Palantir platform, company suggested to health minister
items.summary: US tech company Palantir contacted a health minister about the benefits of adding GP patient data to its national health data tool, documents have revealed.

items.title: Defect notice for blood pressure medication with strength typo
items.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has issued a defect notice for a blood pressure medication which states the incorrect dose on its packaging.

items.title: Mildly low platelets: what should GPs do next?
items.summary: Clinical conundrum: In the next in our series, consultant haematologist Dr Priya Sriskandarajah advises on how to manage a female patient presenting with mildly low platelets on repeat testing who feels well but reports easy bruising A 38-year-old female is called in to discuss repeat blood tests.

items.title: UKHSA concerned over ‘low uptake’ of pharmacy MenB jab offer
items.summary: Less than one in three eligible 18- and 19-year-olds have had a first dose of the free MenB vaccine which is currently being offered in pharmacies. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said this meant more than 580,000 students in this age group had not yet come forward. The government agency said it was concerned...

items.title: Minister assures NHS workforce plan will address need for more community nurses
items.summary: The highly anticipated NHS workforce plan will set out plans for boosting the community nursing workforce, a minister has assured. It comes as several concerns have been raised around a sharp decline in nurses working across the community – including a 49% reduction in district nurses between 2009 and June 2026.

items.title: Easier access to primary care is putting ‘extreme demand’ on waiting list, NHSE says
items.summary: Easier access to primary care is leading to extreme demand for services, NHS England has said. It comes as figures show a record number of patients have been referred to the waiting list for elective care.

items.title: Last chance to register for free Pulse virtual event with sessions on COPD and diabetes
items.summary: GPs have less than a week to register for a free two-day virtual event in November which will feature a talk from NHS England’s national clinical director for prescribing.

items.title: Upcoming Nursing in Practice virtual event to focus on diabetes and respiratory
items.summary: Nurses working in primary care and community settings are being invited to attend a free virtual event focused on diabetes and respiratory conditions next month. Nursing in Practice Virtual: Diabetes and Respiratory takes place on Thursday 3 December.

items.title: Stopping GLP-1s associated with increased risk of heart attack and stroke, study finds
items.summary: Stopping GLP-1 treatment is associated with a substantially increased risk of heart attack, stroke or death, a new study has found.

items.title: Room tidying, list cleansing, dirty tricks
items.summary: Copperfield on how NHS England’s latest attempts to squeeze general practice won’t result in less work for GPs First NHSE came for our patients. Now they’re coming for our waiting rooms. Next it’ll be our lunch money. To explain.

items.title: Drug-facilitated sexual assault: preparing nurses to spot the signs
items.summary: Victims of organised drug-facilitated sexual assault often have no idea what has happened, so it can fall to nurses and other healthcare professionals to notice the signs and ask the right questions – but are they ready?

items.title: Rate of babies born with congenital anomalies in Wales falls
items.summary: The rate of babies born with congenital anomalies in Wales has steadily fallen over recent years, a new report has revealed.

items.title: NHS Property Services installs sensors in 150 GP practices to ‘identify unused space’
items.summary: Exclusive NHS Property Services has installed ‘utilisation sensors’ in around 150 GP practices across England to track how much clinical space is being used, Pulse has learnt.

items.title: BMA pauses consultant strikes as it enters formal negotiations with Government
items.summary: Hospital consultant strikes planned for later this month have been paused, as the BMA and the Government agreed to enter formal negotiations over pay and working conditions.

items.title: RCGP questions NHS England’s claim that GP consultation rooms are underused
items.summary: The RCGP has disputed a claim that GP consultation rooms are underused, arguing that any estimate around practice premises needs to ‘reflect how general practice actually operates’.

items.title: How this nursing associate is breaking down barriers to care for vulnerable patients
items.summary: We caught up with the Nurse/Nursing Team of the Year shortlist ahead of this year’s General Practice Awards, taking place on 4 December at the Novotel London West in Hammersmith.

items.title: Nurse shortages and lack of workforce planning threaten social care reform
items.summary: A growing shortage of registered nurses in social care is creating challenges for specialist providers, while the absence of a long-term workforce plan risks exacerbating pressures in the sector, a report published by the Casey Commission has warned.

items.title: ‘Going into private general practice saved me from leaving medicine altogether’
items.summary: After suffering burnout from eight years as a GP partner in the NHS, Dr Oliver Denton’s move into private practice helped him find his way back to what he loved about the job in the first place From day one as a GP trainee in Gloucestershire my goal was to become a partner.

items.title: Cold-health alert issued for North West and West Midlands regions
items.summary: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued its first cold-health alert of the 2026/27 winter season – warning that low temperatures can result in increased use of health care services.

items.title: ‘Enhanced’ Band 7 health visitor role created after long-running strike action
items.summary: A ‘new and distinct’ Band 7 specialist health visitor role has been created in Wales following nine months of industrial action.

items.title: iHV issues training guide for perinatal and infant mental health
items.summary: A new brochure to provide nurses, health visitors and other practitioners with specialist training information on perinatal and infant mental health has been launched by the Institute of Health Visiting (iHV).

items.title: Civil servant convicted of fraud for holding multiple full-time Government and NHS jobs
items.summary: A former civil servant has been convicted of fraud for obtaining and holding multiple full-time Government jobs at the same time, including at the Department of Health and Social Care and at one NHS trust.

items.title: Long Covid linked to 14% higher risk of developing high blood pressure
items.summary: People diagnosed with long Covid had a 14% higher risk of developing high blood pressure than those without the condition, a new study involving more than 1.2 million adults has found.

items.title: A&G and referrals to remain ‘separate options’ within single point of access, GPs told
items.summary: GP practices in one area have been told they will be able to continue sending advice and guidance (A&G) requests and referrals as separate options via ‘multiple’ single points of access within each trust, covering individual specialties and subspecialties.

items.title: BMA accepts Northern Ireland GP contract offer putting an end to collective action
items.summary: The BMA in Northern Ireland has reached a deal with the Government for the 2026/27 GP contract, including an additional £20m in each of the next two years to support neighbourhood health reforms and ‘improve access’.

items.title: Care home nurses vaccinating residents to help ‘take burden off’ GP practices
items.summary: Care home nurses in Lancashire and South Cumbria are administering vaccinations directly to residents and staff under a new innovative programme.

items.title: One in three people put off GP appointments due to work pressures, Healthwatch finds
items.summary: More than one in three workers in England delayed or avoided going to a GP appointment in the last year because of work commitment or difficulty getting time off, a new survey has found. The research commissioned by Healthwatch England also found that the figure rose to 50% among employees on zero-hours contracts.

items.title: Success of winter plan will ‘rely on whole general practice workforce’
items.summary: Government funding to boost winter capacity in primary care services will only deliver success if practice nurses are placed at the “heart of planning and decision-making”, a union has warned.

items.title: NHSE chair suggests GP practices turn waiting areas into consulting rooms
items.summary: The NHS England chair has suggested GP practices could turn waiting areas into consultation rooms, amid an ongoing review into how the GP estate is used.

items.title: ‘I’m warning my patients about the single patient record – are you?’
items.summary: Dr Paul O’Reilly makes a case against the proposed single patient record, warning that GPs may no longer be able to protect their patients by losing the data controller role As they perceive it, the greatest threat to the liberty of my patients is the efficiency of what they typically experience as a malign…

items.title: Interview: NMC entering ‘new era’ as Paul Rees vows to ‘turn regulator around once and for all’
items.summary: In an exclusive interview with Nursing in Practice, Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) chief executive and registrar Paul Rees reflects on the challenges and changes seen at the regulator over the last year – from the increased registration fee, to lessons learnt from the Letby case, record fitness to practise…

items.title: Patients urged to get vaccinated as data shows flu activity is ‘increasing’
items.summary: Patients eligible for the flu vaccination are being urged by Public Health Wales to get vaccinated as soon as possible following evidence that the flu is circulating.

items.title: Nurse-led clinics could benefit from £40m reallocated funding for GP practices
items.summary: The government has announced that £40m of general practice funding will be reallocated to help provide ‘additional care’ for patients considered most at risk of becoming seriously unwell this winter.

items.title: Money saved through GP list-cleansing drive to fund £40m winter programme
items.summary: A programme for practices to identify and provide additional care to frail patients will be funded via money saved through NHS England’s GP list cleansing drive.

items.title: The UK Shingles vaccination programme – what primary care nurses need to know
items.summary: In the latest in our CPD series, nurse immunisation lead Helen Crosbie outlines the principles and practicalities of the UK shingles vaccination programme for nurses working in primary care, including tips on how to manage common questions about the vaccine. Read the full module on Nursing in Practice 365 today.

items.title: Eye drops used for eye examinations recalled over incorrect expiry date
items.summary: Three batches of eye drops used for eye examinations are being recalled due to being labelled with the incorrect expiry dates, the UK’s medicines watchdog has said.

items.title: GP funding reallocated to keep frail patients out of hospital over winter
items.summary: The Government has announced ring-fenced funding for GP practices to ‘proactively identify’ and provide additional care for patients most at risk of becoming seriously unwell this winter.

items.title: ICB refuses to fund GPs for transitioning patients from discontinued Levemir
items.summary: One ICB has rejected a proposal from GP leaders seeking funding for practices switching patients from Levemir (insulin detemir) to alternatives.

items.title: ‘What next? GP to negotiate world peace?’
items.summary: Dr Reva Gudi offers a tongue-in-cheek defence of general practice, arguing that while specialists have depth, GPs have the breadth to join it all together Reading my clinical correspondence before morning surgery: GP to refer to RACPC (Rapid Access Chest Pain Clinic).

items.title: British healthcare worker being treated for Ebola in London hospital
items.summary: A British healthcare worker has been flown back to the UK for treatment after testing positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The Government confirmed the man, who is believed to be in a stable condition, was brought back to the UK in a planned medical evacuation on Thursday (5 November).

items.title: Patients told to text ‘here’ or ‘gone’ as part of NHS England GP list-cleansing pilot
items.summary: NHS England has introduced a new option for patients to confirm they shouldn’t be removed from their GP practice’s list. Patients can now respond to communications about NHSE’s GP list-cleansing via SMS – texting the words ‘here’ or ‘gone’ – as part of a pilot launched by the commissioner.

items.title: District nurse ‘cuts’ to blame for rising end of life A&E visits, says RCN
items.summary: A decline in district and community nursing roles has led to a rise in people at the end of life having to turn to A&E departments for help, the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has warned. RCN general secretary and chief executive Professor Nicola Ranger said there were now ‘too few’ nurses in the community...

items.title: ‘Primary care nursing has a strong part to play in cancer care’
items.summary: National primary care nursing adviser for cancer charity Macmillan Callum Metcalfe-O’Shea emphasises the role of general practice nurses in prevention, diagnosis, survivorship, and reducing avoidable hospital admissions.

items.title: Primary care ‘lacks involvement’ in supporting transition from child to adult health care
items.summary: Primary care services are ‘not always sufficiently involved’ in the transition pathways to support children moving into adult services, a cross-party parliamentary committee has said.

items.title: GPs lack information to support young people moving to adult services
items.summary: Primary care services are not always ‘sufficiently involved’ in supporting young people with the transition from children to adult health and social care services despite being well-placed to offer continuity, an expert panel has concluded.

items.title: Cancer blood test trial begins in 200 GP practices
items.summary: An NHS trial to test the effectiveness of a blood test to detect a range of cancers is being rolled out across 200 GP practices. More than 20,000 patients will take place in the study to assess whether a blood test can spot prostate, ovarian, bowel, pancreatic, stomach, liver and other abdominal cancers.

items.title: Health news watch: West Nile virus in Europe, Healthwatch retained and more
items.summary: Here, we look at the clinical news that patients might have read in the mainstream media in October and provide the original evidence behind the stories so that you can answer any questions that may come up. Cahal McQuillan reports.

items.title: NMC urged to review title and scope of learning disability nursing
items.summary: The nursing regulator has been urged to examine the title and scope of registration of learning disability nursing amid concerns for the future of the profession.

items.title: Less than three weeks to go until Nursing in Practice North
items.summary: There are less than three weeks to go until our Nursing in Practice North event – with nurses from across the North coming together in Liverpool for a full day of clinical updates, practical learning and networking. Taking place on 25 November at Crowne Plaza Liverpool City Centre, the free event offers up to 5...

items.title: Take-home naloxone to reduce opioid overdose risk – how nurses can improve uptake
items.summary: Advanced nurse practitioner and independent prescriber Nichola Walker and district nurse sister Sian McGraw draw on the findings of a recent clinical audit exploring how to improve uptake of naloxone.

items.title: Can you diagnose this fast-growing, red skin lesion?
items.summary: Our next quick quiz in dermatology asks: what’s this rapidly growing red skin lesion that is painless, but bleeds readily?

items.title: How surgical causes can mimic reflux in infants – and how not to miss them
items.summary: Dilemmas in paediatrics: In the final part in this series, GPwER in paediatrics Dr David Capehorn looks at three surgical diagnoses that can initially resemble infant reflux, and the clinical patterns that should prompt urgent…

items.title: GP practice manager ‘knocking on patient doors’ to prevent list-cleansing removals
items.summary: Exclusive GP practice staff personally ‘knocked on doors’ of patients to ensure they were not removed from patient lists amid a national ‘list-cleansing’ drive. NHS England’s ongoing aggressive list-cleansing exercise is targeting six to seven million patients in total, Pulse has previously revealed.

items.title: Research brings Strep A vaccine ‘a step closer’, says MHRA
items.summary: New research has brought a vaccine against group A streptococcus bacterium (Strep A) a step closer to reality, the UK’s medicines watchdog has said.

items.title: Scheme to support veterans has ‘changed GP practice culture’
items.summary: A scheme which supports GP teams to improve healthcare access for veteran patients has ‘changed practice culture’, a study has suggested.

items.title: Nurses urged to ‘never give up’ on pursuing leadership roles
items.summary: A general practice nurse (GPN) has encouraged nurses to step into leadership roles to help tackle health inequalities.

items.title: Former Royal Navy nurse to honour family and fallen at Cenotaph
items.summary: The Remembrance Sunday march past the Cenotaph in Whitehall this year will feature former Royal Navy nurse Sue Warner, a veteran of the conflicts in the Falkland Islands and Afghanistan.

items.title: How this frailty team is helping older patients stay independent and avoid hospital
items.summary: We caught up with the Nurse/Nursing Team of the Year shortlist ahead of this year’s General Practice Awards, taking place on 4 December at the Novotel London West in Hammersmith.

items.title: Practice nurses urged to champion veteran health scheme
items.summary: In the lead up to Remembrance Day, practice nurses are being encouraged to champion a health scheme to provide the best possible care and treatment for Armed Forces veterans.

items.title: ICBs planning to spend less on neighbourhood services following restructuring, NAO finds
items.summary: Several ICBs are expecting to spend less money on developing neighbourhood health and community services following reductions in running costs, the public spending watchdog has found.

items.title: NHS workforce plan being reassessed due to AI advances, says health secretary
items.summary: The NHS workforce plan has been delayed again because advances in AI has caused the Government to reassess staffing numbers, the health secretary has said.

items.title: Concern practice nurses ‘forgotten’ as health secretary puts focus on GPs
items.summary: Concerns have been raised that nurses working in primary care and community settings have been ‘forgotten’ amid the health secretary’s plans to shift more care into the community.

items.title: Scheme to support veterans has ‘changed GP practice culture’
items.summary: A scheme which supports general practice nurses and teams to improve healthcare access for veteran patients has ‘changed GP practice culture’, a study has suggested.

items.title: District nurses are ‘the linchpin’ of shifting care out of hospitals, minister told
items.summary: The government has once again been warned that its plans to shift care towards the community will be ‘extremely difficult’ without district nurses – a profession that must not be seen as an ‘optional extra’.

items.title: Self-referral to the GMC is classic self harm
items.summary: Copperfield attempts to get to the bottom of why GPs are needlessly referring themselves to the GMC Remember resilience? That was a thing with GPs a while back, wasn’t it? Everyone was being, or was being encouraged to be, resilient. Because that was what you needed to be to survive as a GP.

items.title: NHS England in discussions with GPs about taking over outpatient budget
items.summary: NHS England is in discussions with a group of GPs about practices ‘owning the outpatient budget’, the commissioner’s chief executive has revealed.

items.title: ICB staff cuts risk loss of essential skills, watchdog warns
items.summary: Plans to cut around a third of integrated care board (ICB) staff could leave them without the expertise to deliver long-term improvements in population health, the National Audit Office (NAO) has warned.

items.title: GPs ‘should monitor diabetes risk’ in months after starting patients on antipsychotics
items.summary: Significant metabolic changes are seen in the first 90 days of use of antipsychotic medications, say researchers who recommend closer monitoring at the start.

items.title: Last chance to register for free Pulse LIVE Liverpool event this month
items.summary: GPs have a final chance to register for Pulse LIVE Liverpool, which will cover the latest NICE diabetes guidance, ADHD management and shared care, polypharmacy and the new chickenpox vaccination programme.

items.title: MPs warn of ‘dangerous gaps’ in regulation of cosmetic treatments
items.summary: Failures to regulate cosmetic treatments such as fillers and Botox have exposed consumers to avoidable harm, MPs have warned in a report calling for urgent action to close gaps in safety standards.

items.title: ‘We’ll end up in the wrong place’ if A&G is ‘overused’, warns CMO
items.summary: The NHS will ‘end up in the wrong place’ if GP advice and guidance (A&G) is ‘overused’, England’s chief medical officer has told Pulse.

items.title: Plans to cut community nurses from children’s service dropped
items.summary: Proposals to cut community staff nurses from Suffolk’s Healthy Child Service have been revised by the county council following a public consultation. Suffolk’s Healthy Child Service currently covers health visiting, school nursing and support for young parents.

items.title: NMC officially launches four-year midwifery regulation strategy
items.summary: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) has officially launched its four-year strategy for midwifery regulation, following approval by the regulator’s governing council in September.

items.title: BMA warns GPs against ‘unnecessary’ and ‘erroneous’ GMC self-referrals
items.summary: ‘Unnecessary’ and ‘erroneous’ self-referrals to the GMC are a bigger issue than under-reporting, the BMA has said in new advice to doctors.

items.title: Five-year UK settlement path to remain open to doctors
items.summary: Public service workers including doctors and nurses will still be able to settle in the UK after five years, the Government has announced as part its new ‘earned settlement model’.

items.title: Last chance to register for Pulse LIVE Belfast
items.summary: GPs in Northern Ireland are invited to register for the free Pulse LIVE conference in Belfast next week.

items.title: Government scraps plan for 15-year settlement wait for migrant care workers
items.summary: The Home Office has announced new rules of settlement for migrant care workers following a review of its planned reforms originally set out in November 2025.

items.title: MMRV catch-up call as 15k children with chickenpox consulted by GP
items.summary: A total of 3,037 children and young people were hospitalised with chickenpox in England last year, according to new data from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

items.title: Nurses graduate with more debt than doctors, RCN analysis finds
items.summary: Nursing students in England are graduating with more debt than medical students despite studying for shorter degrees and earning less throughout their careers, new analysis by the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has found.

items.title: GPs warn prescribing budget overhaul could impact patient care
items.summary: GPs have warned that plans to overhaul practice prescribing budgets across three Midlands counties could put pressure on them to cut costs at the expense of patient care.

items.title: ‘Are GPs really best placed to take on long-term management of ADHD?’
items.summary: Dr David Turner reflects on the growing pressures surrounding ADHD diagnosis and management, and why GPs cannot continue to shoulder the burden During GP training, we are taught that the bereaved fluctuate back and forth between five stages: denial, anger bargaining, depression and acceptance.

items.title: Warning over ‘decimated’ community nursing workforce
items.summary: The community nursing workforce has seen a sharp decline across district nursing, health visiting and school nursing services, but a slight increase in nurses working in general practice, according to analysis by the Nuffield Trust.

items.title: Government confirms eligibility for spring 2027 Covid vaccination
items.summary: Covid-19 vaccinations will be offered to adults aged 75 and over, immunosuppressed people aged six months and over, and residents of care homes for older adults in spring 2027, the government has confirmed.

items.title: Renewed chickenpox vaccination appeal after thousands of child hospitalisations
items.summary: A total of 3,037 children and young people were hospitalised with chickenpox in England last year, according to new data from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

items.title: Domperidone prescribing guidance updated over severe hypertension risk
items.summary: A new contraindication for the dopamine receptor antagonist domperidone has been introduced by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), advising that the medicine must no longer be used in patients with confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma due to a risk of severe hypertension.

items.title: NHSE sets out requirements for pharmacy prescribing including GP communication
items.summary: NHS England has set out requirements for pharmacies delivering prescribing services, including sending GP practices information on all prescribing activity.

items.title: Propranolol safety concerns prompt calls for NICE guideline review
items.summary: Pharmacy bodies have sent an open letter to the National Institute of Clinical Excellence (NICE) calling for a review of the clinical guideline for generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults, known as CG113, following patient safety concerns associated with propranolol.

items.title: MHRA approves new oral treatment for plaque psoriasis
items.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has approved a new oral treatment for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over.

items.title: Skincare trends: how nurses can guide children and young people
items.summary: Given the physiological differences in the skin of children and young people compared to adults, elaborate multi-step skincare routines – which have become increasingly popular on social media – can risk damaging the skin barrier rather than protecting it.

items.title: NHS safety investigations body will no longer be abolished, Government confirms
items.summary: The Government is set to reverse its decision to abolish the Health Services Safety Investigations Body (HSSIB) and transfer its investigative functions to the CQC.

items.title: New CQC chief executive takes up post
items.summary: A new CQC chief executive has now taken up post, the watchdog has announced – one year after Sir Julian Hartley resigned over a care quality inquiry.

items.title: Fewer employers making ‘disproportionate’ FtP referrals of ethnic minority doctors, GMC says
items.summary: Fewer employers are referring disproportionate numbers of ethnic minority or internationally qualified doctors to fitness-to-practise tribunals, according to the GMC.

items.title: Acne: Why treatment can fail – and how to improve outcomes
items.summary: As part of our Pulse Live sessions highlights, GPwER in Dermatology Dr Bilal Khan explains why acne can fail to respond to treatment – and how to support improved outcomes Acne is an inflammatory skin disease affecting the pilosebaceous unit (hair follicle, sebaceous gland and arrector pili muscle) which has a chronic…

items.title: Myasthenia gravis: what it is, and when to suspect it
items.summary: Once in a lifetime: Continuing our series on conditions that GPs may only rarely encounter, GP Dr James Chambers considers the rare disorder myasthenia gravis Note details of the case in this article have been altered to ensure anonymity What is myasthenia gravis?

items.title: Cold weather associated with 2,200 deaths in England last year
items.summary: Cold weather was associated with 2,200 deaths in England during winter last year, a new report from the UK Health Security Agency has found. The UKHSA latest cold mortality monitoring report shows that 2,200 deaths were associated with cold weather across five cold weather episodes in 2025/26.

items.title: About 500 GP practices affected by website outage, NHS England confirms
items.summary: NHS England has confirmed that about 500 practices have been affected by disruption to their websites, after a company providing website services entered administration.

items.title: Unions and MPs warn that GP nurses will be ‘left behind’ on pay
items.summary: Calls by some ministers and unions to ringfence GP nursing salaries have gone unanswered by the government and NHS England despite their recommendation to boost pay for GPs and doctors.
